notes.text: Before leaving, check hakonenavi for the ropeway and pirate ship. Both stop in bad weather.
Swimsuits for Yunessun (rental exists but costs extra), a rash guard for anyone with tattoos, warm layers, and the original passports for the snack bar tonight.
Hakone Sushi and Snack Takachan are booked by phone only. Check both are confirmed for 8 before the day starts.

stops.summary: Leftover wagyu rice bowls and coffee, then out the door for the first ropeway.
stops.story: Last night's cook-off leftovers go over rice for the best villa breakfast of the trip. Fuji is clearest early on winter mornings, so this is the morning to move fast.
how: Reheat the wagyu and pile it on rice.
Check hakonenavi for ropeway and boat status.
Tozan bus to Togendai on the Freepass, or two taxis if you miss it.
tips: Togendai is close by car, so two taxis are a cheap fix if the bus timing doesn't work.
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.summary: First car up over the lake to a steaming volcano, with Fuji over the ridge if the sky plays along.
stops.story: The gondolas lift you from Lake Ashi via Ubako up to Owakudani's sulphur vents, and early winter mornings give the best shot at a clear Fuji. You're on the side that's running: the Sounzan section is shut for inspection.
how: Be at Togendai for the first car.
Ride up via Ubako to Owakudani. It's on the Freepass.
tips: The Owakudani–Sounzan leg is closed 7–24 Dec, with a crowded replacement bus. Don't go that way.
Gondolas run continuously, so 8 people is no problem.
wishes: Legendary, not generic: nothing only there because it is on page one of every Tokyo or Kyoto itinerary, and no sit-down sightseeing filler between the big moments

stops.summary: Sulphur steam, rotten-egg air and black eggs: each one supposedly adds 7 years to your life.
stops.story: Owakudani is a live volcanic valley where the ground hisses and the eggs come out boiled black in the hot springs. Eat one each for the legendary 7 extra years, then do the group photo in the steam.
how: Buy black eggs, about ¥500 per 5. Two bags covers 8.
Get the photo with the vents behind you and Fuji over the ridge.
Head back to the ropeway station.
tips: The nature trail needs online advance booking (¥800). Skip it unless someone has already booked.
The ropeway isn't open before 09:00, so the first car up is the earliest you can be here.
wishes: Legendary, not generic: nothing only there because it is on page one of every Tokyo or Kyoto itinerary, and no sit-down sightseeing filler between the big moments

stops.summary: Sail across Lake Ashi on a fake pirate ship. Top deck for Fuji and the red torii from the water.
stops.story: Yes, it's a full-on pirate galleon on a mountain lake, and yes, it's ridiculous. It's 25 minutes across Lake Ashi to Moto-Hakone, with the red torii appearing on the shore as you come in.
how: Walk from the ropeway to the Togendai pier.
Board with the Freepass and head straight for the top deck.
Get off at Moto-Hakone and walk the lakeshore to the shrine.
tips: The first-class deck costs extra. The open top deck has the better view anyway.
It's freezing on deck in December. Wear everything.
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: Cedar steps up to the shrine and the red torii standing in the lake. Shoot it from the side, skip the queue.
stops.story: A red gate stands in the water of Lake Ashi at the bottom of a cedar-lined approach. It's Hakone's signature photo. By midday the queue to stand in it can hit 30–90 minutes, and you have better things to do.
how: Walk the lakeshore from Moto-Hakone to the shrine.
Climb the cedar steps to the main shrine.
Shoot the torii from the side path instead of joining the queue.
tips: If someone insists on the classic shot, one person holds the place in the queue while the rest explore.
Check whether the Peace Torii is closed off. It has been closed for year-end crowds before.
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: Clay-pot rice and a side-dish buffet looking out over the lake you just sailed.
stops.story: Ashinoko Chaya is run by the pirate-ship company: donabe rice and an obanzai side-dish buffet beside Lake Ashi. It's a warm, sit-down refuel before an afternoon in wine and sake baths.
how: Walk back to the Moto-Hakone port area.
Go round the buffet, but don't overload: you're in a swimsuit in an hour.
Take the Tozan bus to Kowakien on the Freepass.
tips: Last entry 15:30, so a lunch at this time is easy.
Opening hours change with the season.
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: Soak in red wine, sake and coffee in your swimsuits. A hot-spring theme park all 8 can do together.
stops.story: Yunessun's wine bath was rebuilt as a fake winery, with vines and barrels, and this season the sake bath uses Nihonsakari daiginjo in the indoor swimsuit zone. It's mixed-gender, so the whole group stays together, and phones are allowed, which means the photos will exist.
how: Buy date-specific e-tickets on yunessun.com in advance, or show the Freepass at the gate for the discount.
Swimsuits on (rental from ¥1,250), then do the wine bath, the sake bath and the coffee bath.
Ask at entry when staff are doing the wine pours today.
tips: Sunday queues of an hour or more are reported. Have the e-tickets ready.
No visible tattoos: cover them with a rash guard. The staff sake-pouring show only starts on 26 Dec, so it's not on today.
Check at the gate that the coffee bath is running. It isn't on the official news pages.
wishes: Yunessun wine, sake and coffee baths in Hakone, and a villa wagyu cook-off on the Hakone night

stops.summary: Crystal arches and a glass Christmas tree lighting up as the dark comes down. In by 17:00.
stops.story: A Venetian-glass garden full of crystal arches and a big glass Christmas tree that catch the light as dusk falls, with candles lit through the 1–25 Dec run. It's Hakone's main December illumination, and you're arriving just as the lights come on.
how: Get in before the 17:00 last entry. Show the Freepass for the discount.
Walk the crystal arches, then the glass tree.
Walk to Hakone Sushi when it closes.
tips: Advance tickets are available online if you want to skip the desk.
It's cold out in the open garden after a hot bath. Dry your hair.
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: Sengokuhara's real sushi place: a father-and-son counter, a tatami room for 8, and sake.
stops.story: Locals call it the sushi place in Sengokuhara: father and son have been behind the counter for decades, and it's full most nights. Reviews rave about the special-grade chirashi (¥3,500), the uni-ikura bowl and the anago.
how: Take the tatami room booked for 8.
Order chirashi, uni-ikura bowls and anago to share, and a round of sake.
Last order is 20:00. Then it's a 14-minute walk to the snack bar.
tips: CHECK: bookings are by phone only (0460-84-7890), not by DM. Confirm the tatami room for 8.
Credit cards accepted.
Omakase runs just under ¥7,000 if anyone wants to go big.
wishes: Everyone stays together; every booking is for 8 at the same table or private room (8名で、同じテーブル/個室)

stops.summary: Take over a mountain-village snack bar: mama-san, karaoke mic, the 8 of you. Hakone's only nightlife.
stops.story: A snack bar is Japan's small-town living room: a mama-san behind the bar, a karaoke machine and regulars who'll judge your song. With 8 of you it turns into a private karaoke party, the most local night out you can get in a village with no other nightlife.
how: Phone 0460-83-8677 the day before. Ask for a set price or nomihodai for 8.
Sing badly and loudly, and buy the mama-san a drink.
Take two taxis back to the villa, booked ahead or ask about the bar's lift.
tips: CHECK: confirm the booking and a set price for 8 beforehand. Snack-bar charges add up fast if you don't.
Ask about pick-up (送迎). They arrange transport for guests.
Bring passports: the drinking age is 20.
wishes: Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly
Be bold: prefer one-of-a-kind, local-run, hard-to-book and group-scale things, and name a safe fallback beside every hard-to-book thing

stops.summary: Last soak in the villa onsen. Pack the overnight bags tonight: check-out is 10:00.
stops.story: One last soak in your own hot spring under the cold mountain sky. Tomorrow you're on the move to Kansai, so wake up already packed.
how: Soak, then pack before you sleep.
Gather leftover drinks and food for the train.
tips: Check-out is 10:00. Don't leave packing for the morning.
